Title: Outstanding female scientist award for Professor Temmerman
NewsSummary: The prize will support a PhD project led by young Kenyan women scientists
NewsContent:
Professor Marleen Temmerman received the Outstanding Female Scientist Award by the European and Developing Countries Clinical Trials Partnership at a ceremony at the Eighth EDCTP Forum in Lusaka, Zambia, on November 8. Professor Temmerman is Chair of the Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology and Director of the Centre of Excellence in Women and Child Health in the Faculty of Health Sciences at the Aga Khan University in East Africa.

The award is given to world-class female scientists residing in sub-Saharan Africa and involved in research on poverty-related diseases, including HIV, tuberculosis, malaria, neglected infectious diseases, diarrhoeal diseases, ebola virus disease and yellow fever.

It consists of a recognition trophy and a cash prize that can be used to further the research programmes of the award winner.

"I am very humbled and honoured to receive the EDCTP's Outstanding Female Scientist Award, which I accept proudly on behalf of our research community in Europe and Africa, who has done great work in the area of HIV/AIDS in women and children," said Professor Temmerman.

"I believe that mentoring young researchers is an investment and it can make a big difference. The prize will support a PhD project, led by young Kenyan women scientists, on reducing the consequences of unsafe sex in young girls, such as HIV, sexually transmitted infections and unwanted pregnancies.," she added

A scientist, author and politician, Professor Temmerman has a strong academic background with over 500 publications and books; many PhD students in Europe, Africa, Latin America and China; and several awards and honours.

In 2010, she received the BMJ Lifetime Achievement Award, which recognises outstanding contribution to medicine and healthcare.

Recently, she was awarded the prestigious Marie Popelin award 2016 in Belgium, in recognition of her endeavours for women's rights.

Professor Temmerman is also one of the authors of the new Global Strategy for Women's, Children's and Adolescents' Health that is designed to help achieve Goal 3 of the Sustainable Development Goals, requiring countries to ensure good health and well-being for people of all ages. AKU has pledged to invest more than US$ 85 million over the next decade in support of the Global Strategy.

EDCTP is a partnership of European and sub-Saharan countries supported by the European Union to fund research against HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria and neglected infectious diseases. Its awards recognise outstanding individuals and research teams from Africa and Europe who have made significant achievements and also contributed to EDCTP's objectives of strengthening clinical research capacity in Africa and supporting South-South and North-South networking.
